LD 312 - An Act Regarding the Rates of Speed at Which School Buses Travel

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing

Committee on Transportation. I am present today to introduce LD 312 - An Act Regarding the

'

Rates of Speed at Which School Buses Travel.

.

My name is Gregory Swallow. I proudly represent House District 7 which includes Houlton,

"
Linneus, Ludlow, New limerick and Oakfield.

. _

The purpose of LD 312 is to make changes under Title 29-A (Motor Vehicles and Traftic), Chapter l9, Subchapter 1, Section 2074, Paragraphs D and E. This change would allow school
buses to travel at the posted speed limit when transporting pupils. Currently, school buses are limited to 45 miles per hour when transporting pupils to and from school.

The contention by the school bus drivers and supervisors is that by limiting the speed limit to 45 miles per hour, the probability of an accident is enhanced rather than limited. This danger is further amplified in winter months when buses are "holding back" logging trucks etc. under more treacherous driving conditions. The truck drivers are pushing to pass the bus and taking
chances that they may not otherwise choose if the bus were travelling at the posted speed limit.
Obviously, if the road conditions were so severe that they warranted lower speeds for all parties the bus drivers would use their discretion.

Therefore, the contention for this bill is that though current law is well intended it falls short of its
goal. There are those following me that can offer experiences that will give this issue a more
personal perspective in sharing their real life driving experiences.

10044390:
Joseph Fagnant RSU 29, Houlton LD 312
Dear Members of the Transportation Committee,
I am in support of passing LD 312 (Representative Swallow, Senator Stewart), An Act Regarding the Rates of Speed at Which School Buses Travel. As the superintendent in RSU 29, we often see safety issues around our buses as we are at the crossroads of major roads such as US Highway 1 and US Rt 2. These roads have posted speed limits above the 45 mph limitations currently in law.
Our drivers should be able to travel the speed limit as posted in order to follow the flow of traffic, and be able to move at the same rate of speed as other large vehicles, including trailer trucks and log trucks. By limiting our buses to 45 mph, there is cause for concern as vehicles pile up behind a slower vehicle. This also creates impatient drivers, with the potential for passing erratically, or passing when a bus comes to a stop to deliver students, passing while the stop arm is deployed.
This bill does allow for following the posted speed limit. Please support LD 312, and I think you for your time and attention to this matter.

passing. But the road to Danforth and beyond has no such opportunities for that

in areas that traffic is not coming and they have the chance to get by and back in the
